title: Sunny and the Lorikeet Rainbow | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka discovers a whole flock of rainbow lorikeets roosting in a moonlit grevillea tree, each one a small sleeping bundle of impossible colour dreaming of nectar and flowers. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The tree was full of colour.

Even in the moonlight — even with everything toned down to silver and dark — Sunny could see the colours. Red. Blue. Green. Orange. Small sleeping bundles of it, packed into the branches of the grevillea tree so tightly that the whole tree seemed to glow.

Lorikeets. A whole roosting flock.

She walked slowly under the tree and looked up.

They were all asleep — beaks tucked, feet gripping the branches, each one a small tight ball of extraordinary colour. Some had their heads turned to one side. Some were pressed so close together they were sharing warmth. Little clusters of two and three and four, packed in among the branches like hanging Christmas baubles.

She thought: they spend all day being the loudest, most colourful thing in the bush, and at night they just quietly go to sleep, like everyone else.

One of them made a tiny sleep sound — a small mumble, almost a chirp — and settled deeper into its feathers.

She smiled.

She sat down under the tree.

All around her, just above her head, the most colourful creatures in the whole bush were quietly, peacefully, completely asleep.

She looked up at them for a long time.

Then she closed her eyes too.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, lorikeet rainbow. Goodnight, little one.
